lead: Pennsylvania plumbing deals with old housing, cold winters and many private wells. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers from Philadelphia to Pittsburgh.
risk: aging pipes in older homes, frozen pipes and private wells
risk_short: old pipes, frozen pipes and wells
why: Pennsylvania has one of the oldest housing stocks in the country. Philadelphia rowhouses and Pittsburgh homes often have galvanized supply lines, cast-iron drains and lead service lines. Pittsburgh's hills also make sewer laterals long and steep.

Cold winters freeze pipes, and heavy rain floods basements. Many rural homes rely on private wells and septic systems. Pennsylvania has no statewide plumber license; Philadelphia, Pittsburgh and other localities license plumbers.
tips: Insulate basement and wall pipes before winter.
Ask your utility about your service line.
Test your sump pump each spring.
areas: Calls come from Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Allentown, Erie, Reading, Scranton, Harrisburg, Lancaster and rural Pennsylvania.

faq.q: Do plumbers need a license in Pennsylvania?
faq.a: There is no statewide plumber license. Philadelphia, Pittsburgh and many other municipalities license plumbers, and contractors doing home improvement work must register with the state attorney general's office.
